Try itPredict how steering turns the AV: the turn rate

Goal: know how fast a steering angle turns the AV. Its heading \(\theta\) (rad, counterclockwise from \(x\)) changes at the turn rate \(\dot\theta\) (a dot is a rate of change in time). With the speed \(v\) (m/s), the front wheel angle \(\delta\) (rad, positive turns left) and the wheelbase \(L\):

\[ \dot\theta = \frac{v}{L}\tan\delta \]
  • Faster, or more steering: the heading turns faster.
  • A longer car (larger \(L\)) turns slower at the same angle.
  • Per meter driven, the heading turns \(\dot\theta / v = \tan\delta / L\): that is the curvature \(\kappa\), the turn per meter. So a fixed \(\delta\) drives a circle (next panel).
